deployment_note: Provider dashboards and alert routes require account access and an owned notification destination. This reviewed specification does not claim they are live.

privacy.ip_strategy: omit-or-pseudonymize unless incident response requires full address
privacy.path_strategy: use route templates/classes; never retain reset tokens, IDs, or secrets embedded in paths
privacy.user_agent_strategy: classify at the provider or controlled processor and discard raw values when practical

dashboard_specs.provider_surface: Cloudflare Security Analytics and Security Events
widgets: matches by rule and action over time
challenge issued, solved, failed, and solve rate by rule
country and ASN aggregates without exporting full client IP by default
origin response status and cache status
dashboard_specs.promotion_use: Export and reviewer-label bounded JSONL, then run analyze_security_events.py. Dashboard counts alone cannot authorize enforcement.

dashboard_specs.provider_surface: Protected API CSP collector and log analytics
dashboard_specs.promotion_use: Run analyze_csp_reports.py; never auto-add a reported source to policy.
Operational health only; a clean dashboard does not replace plan review or protected apply approval.

alerts.note: Tune to the measured baseline; do not use a guessed global percentage.
Correlate with origin latency and provider health before changing WAF policy.
Traffic spikes are not automatically attacks; correlate with cache, bot and WAF signals.
Relevant only after a dynamic authentication origin is routed through the edge.
A high solve rate can indicate false positives; a low solve rate can indicate automation.
Corroborate before quarantine or deny; provider reputation alone is insufficient.
Correlate with deploys, cache-policy changes, traffic mix, and origin load.
Check edge transforms, application CSP, cache variants, and direct-origin bypass.
Reconcile emergency dashboard changes into code or revert them before the next apply.
Do not treat one cached resolver as proof of an outage.
